$comment: E86 (PR-106): one agent tool of the registry, devos/agents/<id>.json. scripts/devos/tools.mjs checks the same rules (tools.mjs check) and reads the files; this schema is for editors and for anyone adding a tool.
title: DEV_OS agent tool

id.description: The tool's id, as devos.config.json's agents name it; the file is <id>.json.

name.description: Its short name in the run's notes: "the Cursor CLI".

label.description: Its full name in prompts: "Claude Code".

provider.description: The AI service it calls, when it is one.

commands.description: Every name the CLI goes by, the command among them: a usage record or a progress line names the tool by any of them.

install.description: An npm package, or a package downloaded from url and checked by the SHA-256 in tool_versions.<id> (PR-93), whose version is always tool_versions.<id>; or none (E87): a command already on the runner, such as node running the tool's own script under devos/agents/<id>/.

effort.description: flag: the developer's effort is passed ({effort}); model: the model's name holds it; none: the tool takes none.

efforts.description: The levels a flag takes; empty otherwise.

fast.description: Whether a pool entry may set fast.

can.description: E87 (PR-109): what the tool can do. headless: it runs from a prompt with no person there; edit: it writes files; shell: it runs commands. The builder and the reviewer need all three, a planner headless and edit.

parser.description: The output format it writes, which the runner reads; contract (E87): the tool writes the agent output contract itself (scripts/devos/agent-result.mjs).

answer.description: schema: the CLI takes the answer's schema ({schema}); file: the prompt asks for the answer in a file.

stdin.description: true: the prompt goes on standard input; false: the command line names its file ({prompt}).

secret.description: The GitHub secret of the first account; <secret>_2 is the second's. A project's own tool uses DEVOS_AGENT_KEY (E87): every AI job's caller names it.

env.description: The job's names for the two accounts: <env>_1 and <env>_2.

cli.description: The name the CLI reads its credential from.

alt.description: An alternative credential (Claude Code's API key): secret, env and cli.

unset.description: Names cleared before an account's credential is set.

account.description: The repository variable that picks the first account (1 or 2).

setup.description: What the tool needs before it runs: env values and files copied into $HOME.

kits.description: Per role (builder, reviewer, planner): the files moved aside and the role's files put in their place (role-env.mjs).

run.description: Each role's arguments after the command, with {model}, {effort}, {turns}, {schema}, {last} and {prompt}; models: the arguments that list its models.
